cities.name: Gangtok
cities.overview: Sikkim's capital, strung along a ridge at about 1,650 m with views of Kangchenjunga on clear mornings and a pedestrian-only MG Marg at its heart.
cities.history: It became the capital of the Buddhist kingdom of Sikkim in the 19th century, and it grew as a stop on the trade route to Tibet. Sikkim joined India in 1975.

cities.name: Lachung
cities.overview: A mountain village at about 2,700 m in North Sikkim, the overnight base for Yumthang Valley. Visits need a permit arranged through a registered tour operator.

cities.name: Pelling
cities.overview: A hill town in west Sikkim with close-up views of Kanchenjunga, and old monasteries nearby.

cities.name: Namchi
cities.overview: The main town of south Sikkim, with giant hilltop statues of Shiva and Guru Padmasambhava.

cities.name: Yuksom
cities.overview: A historic village, once the first capital of Sikkim, and the starting point of the Goecha La trek.

cities.name: Ravangla
cities.overview: A small town in south Sikkim known for its Buddha Park.

cities.name: Dzuluk
cities.overview: A small hamlet on the old Silk Route, with zigzag roads in east Sikkim.

places.name: Rumtek Monastery
places.shortDescription: The largest monastery in Sikkim and a seat of the Karma Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism.
places.description: Rumtek sits on a hillside about 24 km from Gangtok, facing the town across the valley. Its main prayer hall is richly painted with murals and thangkas, and the Golden Stupa holds relics of the 16th Karmapa. Monks chant in the hall in the mornings and afternoons. The monastery also houses a college for Buddhist studies. Carry a photo ID, as there is a security check at the gate.
places.history: The 16th Karmapa, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, rebuilt Rumtek in the 1960s after leaving Tibet, on the site of an older monastery from the 18th century.
places.bestTimeNote: March to May and October to December for clear skies.

places.name: Tsomgo Lake
places.shortDescription: A glacial lake at 3,753 m on the road to Nathu La, frozen in winter and ringed by rhododendrons in spring.
places.description: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake lies in a high bowl about 40 km from Gangtok on the road to the Nathu La pass. The oval lake changes colour with the seasons, from frozen white in winter to deep blue in summer, and is held sacred by local Sikkimese. Yak rides and tea stalls line the shore. Visitors need a protected-area permit, arranged by Gangtok tour operators, and the altitude can cause breathlessness, so avoid exertion.
places.history: The lake is fed by melting snow from the surrounding mountains. The road beyond it leads to Nathu La on the India–China border, once part of a trade route between Sikkim and Tibet.
places.bestTimeNote: March to May for flowers, October to December for clear views; the road may close after heavy snow.

entryFee.note: Permit required (arranged by registered tour operators in Gangtok); foreigners may visit with a permit.

location.address: Tsomgo Lake, Jawaharlal Nehru Road, East Sikkim, Sikkim

places.name: Yumthang Valley
places.shortDescription: The Valley of Flowers of Sikkim, a high meadow that bursts into rhododendron and primula blooms in spring.
places.description: Yumthang Valley lies at about 3,560 m, 25 km north of Lachung, with the Lachung River running through meadows ringed by snow peaks. In April and May the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary along the way turns pink, red and white with dozens of species in flower. Hot springs lie near the river. Most visitors stay overnight in Lachung on a permit tour from Gangtok, continuing to Zero Point in good weather.
places.history: The Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary was set up in 1984 to protect the valley's exceptional diversity of rhododendrons.
places.bestTimeNote: April to June for flowers; October–November for clear skies. Landslides can close roads in the monsoon.

entryFee.note: Permit required, arranged by registered tour operators in Gangtok.

location.address: Yumthang Valley, Lachung, Mangan district, Sikkim

places.name: Enchey Monastery
places.shortDescription: A 1909 Nyingma monastery on a ridge above Gangtok, known for its annual masked dance.
places.description: A small colourful monastery among pine trees, with views of Kanchenjunga on clear days. The Chaam dance is held each winter.

places.name: Nathu La
places.shortDescription: A high pass on the old Silk Route between Sikkim and Tibet, at the Chinese border.
places.description: Soldiers from both sides stand a few metres apart at the top. Only Indian citizens may visit, with a permit.
places.bestTimeNote: Open only to Indian citizens on certain days, with a permit arranged through a registered operator.

places.name: Fambong Lho Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A 51 sq km forest sanctuary just outside Gangtok, with oaks, orchids and red pandas.
places.description: A close, little-visited forest for birdwatching and day walks, with some short trails and log huts.

places.name: Kyongnosla Alpine Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A high alpine reserve around Tsomgo Lake, known for its rare orchids and rhododendrons.
places.description: A strip of high forest and alpine meadow along the Nathu La road. Its rare plants are at their best in spring and summer.
places.bestTimeNote: This area needs a protected area permit, usually arranged through a registered tour operator in Gangtok.

places.name: Gurudongmar Lake
places.shortDescription: One of the highest lakes in the world, at over 5,000 m in north Sikkim, sacred to Buddhists and Sikhs.
places.description: A huge turquoise lake in a bare plateau close to the Tibetan border, reached on an early-morning drive from Lachen. Altitude is a real concern.
places.bestTimeNote: This area needs a protected area permit, usually arranged through a registered tour operator in Gangtok.

places.name: Pemayangtse Monastery
places.shortDescription: One of Sikkim's oldest and most important monasteries, near Pelling, with a remarkable wooden model of heaven.
places.description: A Nyingma monastery on a ridge facing Kanchenjunga. Its top floor holds a seven-tiered carved wood model of Guru Rinpoche's celestial palace.

places.name: Rabdentse Ruins
places.shortDescription: The ruins of the second capital of the Kingdom of Sikkim, destroyed by Gurkhas in 1814.
places.description: A forest walk leads to stone walls and chortens on a ridge, with sweeping views of the mountains.
places.history: The capital from 1670 until it was overrun in the 1814 Gurkha invasion.

places.name: Khecheopalri Lake
places.shortDescription: A sacred wish-fulfilling lake in west Sikkim, where it's said birds keep the surface clear of leaves.
places.description: A still green lake in a forest bowl, sacred to Buddhists and Hindus. Prayer flags and small wooden walkways lead to the water.

places.name: Tashiding Monastery
places.shortDescription: A Nyingma monastery on a hilltop, 27 km from Gyalshing, with some of the most sacred chortens in Sikkim.
places.description: Said to cleanse sins merely by sight, it's the site of the Bumchu Festival, in which a holy water vessel is opened each year.

places.name: Khangchendzonga National Park
places.shortDescription: India's only mixed UNESCO World Heritage Site, around the world's third-highest mountain.
places.description: A huge park of glaciers, alpine meadows and forest, with red pandas and snow leopards. Treks start from Yuksom, and permits are needed.
places.bestTimeNote: This area needs a protected area permit, usually arranged through a registered tour operator in Gangtok.

places.name: Goecha La
places.shortDescription: A high pass facing Kanchenjunga's south-east face, the goal of Sikkim's most famous trek.
places.description: A multi-day trek from Yuksom through rhododendron forest and alpine meadows, ending in one of the closest views of the world's third-highest peak.
places.bestTimeNote: This area needs a protected area permit, usually arranged through a registered tour operator in Gangtok.

places.name: Ravangla Buddha Park
places.shortDescription: A hilltop park in south Sikkim, with a giant 130-foot statue of the Buddha at Tathagata Tsal.
places.description: Well-kept gardens surround a giant copper Buddha statue, with snowy peaks behind it. Ralang Monastery is close by.

places.name: Namchi Char Dham
places.shortDescription: A hill complex near Namchi, with replicas of India's four great pilgrim shrines and a huge Shiva statue.
places.description: A big pilgrim centre, crowned by a giant Shiva, and in the same town you'll find a giant statue of Guru Padmasambhava at Samdruptse.

places.name: Dzuluk
places.shortDescription: A hamlet at 9,400 ft on the old Silk Route in east Sikkim, famous for its zigzag roads.
places.description: A hair-raising drive of dozens of hairpin bends across a high ridge. Thambi View Point gives a wide view of the road and Kanchenjunga.
places.bestTimeNote: This area needs a protected area permit, usually arranged through a registered tour operator in Gangtok.
